recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not edit the active current ValueSet source for this issue; any future concern about regenerating historical R4B download artifacts should be handled in the generation tooling path, which HL7/kindling#69 already addressed for this issue family.
issue_request: FHIR-35784 was Published/Persuasive for R4B and asked that contained ConceptMaps in the generated valuesets.xml download use the R4/R4B ConceptMap target element <equivalence> and R4 equivalence codes such as wider and narrower, not the R5 <relationship> element and source-is-* relationship codes.
initial_application: No FHIR core source commit explicitly tagged FHIR-35784 was found. The Jira comment links HL7/kindling#69, merged 2022-04-07, whose body says generated instances should use the correct base-standard version when generating R4B and explicitly lists FHIR-35783 and FHIR-35784. In the current FHIR checkout, tools/history/release4b/valuesets.xml was last introduced/updated by core commit cdc3309868 as part of the R4/R5 conversion framework and already has the R4/R4B form.
additional_context: FHIR-35783 is the direct sibling for conceptmaps.xml and cites the same Kindling PR. FHIR-32816 reports the same invalid contained ConceptMap pattern for the nhin-purposeofuse ValueSet in valuesets.xml. The active current source/valueset/valueset-nhin-purposeofuse.xml uses <relationship> and source-is-* codes because the current R5/R6 ConceptMap structure uses those names; changing it to <equivalence> would regress the current specification. The checked release5 valuesets.xml likewise uses the R5 relationship form, while the checked release4b valuesets.xml uses equivalence/wider/narrower. No Zulip or Confluence evidence was found that changes this conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No FHIR source change is needed because the current source is correct for the current build and the checked R4B history valuesets.xml no longer contains the invalid relationship/source-is-* pattern identified by the issue.
